| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="nc">Box</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">&#95;fieldProbeAutoController</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">ShaderFieldAutoController</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | The per-frame controller installed by `Box.fieldProbeAutoControl`, or `null`. Kept on the box so a re-run can stop the previous one before installing its replacement — which is exactly what `fieldProbeAutoControl` does, and why re-running a box does not leave two controllers fighting over the same push constants. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="nc">Box</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">&#95;fieldStatsBinding</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">ShaderFieldStatsBinding</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | How this box is joined to a `ShaderFieldStats` block: the stats object plus whether this box is its *producer* (it owns the buffers and its GLSL records into them) or merely a consumer. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="nc">Once</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">vertex</span> <span class="k">by</span> <span class="nc">Onceing</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | `once.vertex { …GLSL… }` fills the box's `Box.vertex` property from code, the first time only. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="nc">Once</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">fragment</span> <span class="k">by</span> <span class="nc">Onceing</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | `once.fragment { …GLSL… }` fills `Box.fragment` once from code. Same fragment-ordering trap as `Once.vertex`: seed it in a fragment *before* the one that expands `moduleHere`. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="nc">Once</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">vertex&#95;fragment</span> <span class="k">by</span> <span class="nc">Onceing</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | `once.vertex_fragment { …Slang… }` fills `Box.vertex_fragment` once — the shared-Slang route, which overrides whatever `once.vertex`/`once.fragment` put in place. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="nc">Once</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">compute</span> <span class="k">by</span> <span class="nc">Onceing</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | `once.compute { …GLSL… }` fills `Box.compute` once, ahead of the `computeModuleHere` fragment. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="nc">Once</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">task</span> <span class="k">by</span> <span class="nc">Onceing</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | `once.task { …GLSL… }` fills `Box.task` once, ahead of the `meshModuleHere` fragment. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="nc">Once</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">mesh</span> <span class="k">by</span> <span class="nc">Onceing</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | `once.mesh { …GLSL… }` fills `Box.mesh` once, ahead of the `meshModuleHere` fragment. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="nc">Once</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">raygen</span> <span class="k">by</span> <span class="nc">Onceing</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | `once.raygen { …GLSL… }` fills `Box.raygen` once, ahead of the `rayTracingModuleHere` fragment. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="nc">Once</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">miss</span> <span class="k">by</span> <span class="nc">Onceing</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | `once.miss { …GLSL… }` fills `Box.miss` once; leave it unset to build a pipeline with no miss stage at all. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="nc">Once</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">closesthit</span> <span class="k">by</span> <span class="nc">Onceing</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | `once.closesthit { …GLSL… }` fills `Box.closesthit` once. Optional stage. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="nc">Once</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">anyhit</span> <span class="k">by</span> <span class="nc">Onceing</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | `once.anyhit { …GLSL… }` fills `Box.anyhit` once. Optional stage. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="nc">Once</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">intersection</span> <span class="k">by</span> <span class="nc">Onceing</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | `once.intersection { …GLSL… }` fills `Box.intersection` once. Optional stage. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="nc">Once</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">callable</span> <span class="k">by</span> <span class="nc">Onceing</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | `once.callable { …GLSL… }` fills `Box.callable` once. Optional stage. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="nc">Box</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">shaderTemplate</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">MutableMap</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="nc">Any</span><span class="p">&gt;</span></code> | The named values this box's `{{ slot }}` template expressions resolve against — the mechanism behind the shadertoy preamble and any GLSL boilerplate you would rather write once. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="nc">Box</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">stackAutoShaderSources</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">MutableMap</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">&gt;</span></code> | StackSL source, by `stack.auto` slot name, for every `{{ stack.auto.foo }}` this box's shaders declare. Concurrent, because the compile/reload path reads it off the main thread. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">defaultVertexShader</span></code> | The vertex shader a box gets if `moduleHere` expands and the box has no vertex source of its own: one `vec3 pos` input transformed by a `push_constant` block of two `mat4`s, `p` and `m`. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">defaultFragmentShader</span></code> | The fragment shader a box gets if `moduleHere` expands with no fragment source of its own: a flat warm orange, chosen so "it drew *something*" is unmistakable. Declares no uniforms, so it generates no accessors. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">shadertoyVertexShader</span></code> | The vertex shader `shadertoyHere` seeds: no inputs at all, just a full-screen triangle synthesised from `gl_VertexIndex`. That is why the shadertoy module needs a 3-vertex mesh and no vertex buffer. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">shadertoyFragmentShader</span></code> | The fragment shader `shadertoyHere` seeds: the `{{ shadertoy.fragmentPreamble }}` slot (which brings in the `iResolution`/`iTime`/`iMouse`/… uniform block and the `#define`s that make them look like shadertoy globals), a `main` that calls `mainImage`, and a placeholder `mainImage` drawing a uv gradient that pulses with `iTime`. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="nc">Box</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">customTextureResolver</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="nc">Box</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">-</span></code> | A hook for deciding yourself what a shader's `sampler2D someName` should be bound to, consulted before Field's own by-name search of the box's properties. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">defaultRaygenShader</span></code> | The ray-generation shader a box gets when `rayTracingModuleHere` expands and the box has no `raygen` source: it writes the launch uv into the ray payload and traces nothing at all. |

class="nc">Long</span><span class="p">)</span></code>

One `#include` that landed inside a registered include root, handed to a [`ShaderIncludeRootResolver`](graphics.md#shaders-kt-shaderincluderootresolver) to turn into text.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">root</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | The registered root name that matched — the first path segment of a `root/…` include, or, for a relative include, the root the *including* file itself came from. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">includePath</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | The path within `root`, normalised: separators unified to `/`, `.` and empty segments dropped, `..` resolved (and rejected if it would escape the root), no leading slash. This is the key a resolver should look up. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">requestedPath</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | Exactly what the `#include` said, root prefix and all. Useful in diagnostics; do not resolve against it. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">requestingSourcePath</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | The resolved path of the file doing the including (a previous resolution's `resolvedPath`, or a `field/<box>-<id>/<property>.glsl` name for box source), or `null` when shaderc did not supply one. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">includeType</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">ShaderIncludeType</span></code> | `RELATIVE` for `#include "…"`, `STANDARD` for `#include <…>`. Only `RELATIVE` includes are resolved relative to `requestingSourcePath`'s directory. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">includeDepth</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Long</span></code> | How deep this include is nested, straight from shaderc. Informational — nothing in Field enforces a limit on it. |

### ShaderIncludeRootResolver { #shaders-kt-shaderincluderootresolver }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="k">interface</span> <span class="nc">ShaderIncludeRootResolver</span></code>

Turns an include inside one registered root into source text. Register one under a name with `registerShaderIncludeRoot` and every `#include "thatName/whatever.glsl"` in every box's shaders goes through it.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">resolve</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">request</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">ShaderIncludeRootRequest</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">ShaderIncludeResolution</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | Resolve one include, or return `null` if this root does not have it (which the caller turns into a hard error). |

Where a URL-backed include root keeps its on-disk copies, and how patient it is with the network.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">cacheDirectory</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Path</span></code> | Directory the fetched includes are mirrored into, one file per include path. Created on demand. Resolved to an absolute, normalised path, and includes that would escape it are rejected — a remote server cannot talk you into writing outside this directory. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">connectTimeoutMillis</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | `HttpURLConnection` connect timeout, in milliseconds. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">readTimeoutMillis</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | `HttpURLConnection` read timeout, in milliseconds. Both timeouts are felt by whichever thread is compiling — the main runloop, on the reload path — so the defaults are deliberately short. |

How `Box.fieldProbeAutoControl` turns probe read-backs into controller updates: when a batch is big enough to act on, what counts as clipped, and where the diagnostics card goes.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">minSamples</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | Minimum samples in a read-back before the controller is allowed to learn from it. A snapshot with fewer is skipped entirely — `tick()` returns `null` and nothing is applied. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">clipLower</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | Values at or below this (within `clipEpsilon`) count as clipped low and are reported to the controller as a clip rate; `null` means "nothing clips at the bottom". |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">clipUpper</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | Values at or above this (within `clipEpsilon`) count as clipped high; `null` means nothing clips at the top. With both bounds `null` the reported clip rate is a flat `0.0`. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">clipEpsilon</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span></code> | Tolerance for the two clip comparisons — floating-point slop, not a percentage. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">useNominalParams</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code> | `true` applies the controller's *nominal* parameters, `false` (the default) its *applied* ones, which carry the small dither the controller needs to identify the system. Turn it on once identification has settled and the dither is visible in the output. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">displayChannel</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | Box output channel for the HTML diagnostics table (nominal vs applied parameters, objective, confidence, clip rate, p10/p50/p90). `null` disables the display entirely, which is what a headless test wants. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">closeDisplayOnStop</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code> | Whether `stop()` closes the display channel by default. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">clearDisplayOnStop</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code> | Whether `stop()` clears the display channel's contents by default. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">runloopKeySuffix</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | Prefix of the runloop hook key, which is `"$runloopKeySuffix:${box.id}"`. Two controllers on one box need two different values here or the second silently displaces the first. |

The running loop that closes a shader's feedback circuit: read the probe, push the samples into an adaptive controller, hand the new parameters to your `apply` lambda, and draw the diagnostics.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">box</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Box</span></code> | The box this controller belongs to: the source of the display channel and the identity in the runloop hook key. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">probe</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">ShaderFieldProbe</span></code> | The probe being read. `Box.fieldProbeAutoControl` has already put it into continuous-read mode, so it delivers a snapshot every frame rather than at the display rate. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">controller</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">AdaptiveDistributionController</span></code> | The adaptive controller doing the actual learning; its `parameterNames` label the diagnostics table and its `pushSamples` is what turns a batch into parameters. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">config</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">ShaderProbeAutoControlConfig</span></code> | The thresholds, clip bounds and display settings this controller was built with. Read on every tick, but the object is immutable — copy it and rebuild to change your mind. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">tickCount</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | How many ticks have actually done work. Ticks that found no new snapshot, or too few samples, do not count — so a `tickCount` stuck at zero means the probe is not delivering, not that the hook is missing. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">lastBatch</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FieldProbeScalarBatch</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | The last probe batch the controller learned from, or `null` before the first useful tick. Carries both the raw snapshot and the clip rate computed from `config`. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">lastOutput</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">ControlOutput</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | The last controller output — nominal and applied parameters plus diagnostics — or `null` before the first useful tick. The same object the `apply` lambda was handed. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">tick</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">ControlOutput</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | Do one control step, returning the controller's output, or `null` if there was nothing to do. |

## stacksl.kt { #stacksl-kt }

Host-side entry points for StackSL: compiling the stack language to GLSL, and evaluating it on
the GPU sample by sample. The language, its compiler and its diagnostics live in
`afield.stacksl`; this file is the Kotlin surface a box calls.

`stackSL` holds a box's StackSL source, falling back to a parent box's. `compileStackSL`,
`stackSLToGlsl` and the standalone `slGlsl` are pure compilation and need no device. `slEval` and
`slSweep` actually run the compiled function: they wrap it in a small compute shader and dispatch
it through a `Renderer` that defaults to `fromContext()`, so they need a live graphics context.
Neither binds any texture sampler, so a source that needs one is rejected.

`slSweep` returns a [`StackSLSweep`](graphics.md#stacksl-kt-stackslsweep), which implements `ToHTML` and draws itself as an inline SVG
plot of the four output channels with per-channel min/median/max; `StackSLSweep.h` is that HTML.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/stdlib/stacksl.kt`

**Used in:** [StackSL cheatsheet](../stacksl_cheatsheet.md), [StackSL examples](../stacksl_examples.md)

## voronoi.kt { #voronoi-kt }

Practical 3D Voronoi and approximate 3D multiplicatively weighted Voronoi
("CircularDirichlet") for Kotlin + Field linalg.

- voronoi3d(...) builds convex polyhedral cells by intersecting pairwise
  bisector half-spaces, then closing unbounded cells against a large clip box.
- CircularDirichlet3d.build(...) extracts approximate support patches on
  bisector spheres / planes by clipping a sampled surface mesh with the
  weighted score predicate.

The weighted contourer is renderer-oriented: it prefers stable, wound
boundary loops over exact symbolic patch topology.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/stdlib/voronoi.kt`
